question: Which document, slice, schema, format, diagnostic and application contracts should own external document imports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
trigger: User requests harsh honest feedback on a supplied document-conversion audit after implementation closure.
requirements: Preserve format-owned operations, canonical schema authority, observable loss and exact fragment boundaries.
Separate a failed final AI result from a prior usable preview; implement truthful DOCX cancellation and application comment adoption.
Earn each public noun independently; cut wrappers without erasing information or encoded-type inference.
Distinguish ordinary Word review from exact native-state round trips before changing DOCX attachment policy.
Assess and record only; do not implement the supplied audit or promote source findings into browser, bundle or native-artifact proof.
evidenceReuse: Reconciled the latest vocabulary/doctrine reviews and subsequent implementation. Retained their exact historical receipts, then traced current source and ran three focused HappyDOM source probes. Two bounded read-only source investigations checked DOCX/native fidelity and persistence/inference. No new external research or fresh performance measurement.
summary: Pursue corrected design and targeted repair, not the supplied S1-S8 plan as written. Consolidate HTML ingress; fix fragment fitting, silent inline Markdown truncation, AI final-output validity, DOCX cancellation and comment adoption. Reject nullable-only transfer results when they erase observable loss. Detached HTML projection assertion already exists. DOCX native metadata has a live trusted reader and tested independent fidelity; assess explicit attachment rather than blanket deletion. Flatten persistence declarations while retaining encoded-output inference and admission/version laws. Detached DOCX compilation currently activates a full editor. Reopen blanket implementation closure only for these uncovered claims; keep the format-owned public vocabulary and bounded historical proof.

reconciliation.reason: The three new probes reproduce untested HTML and inline Markdown defects; source tracing finds uncovered AI, DOCX and copied-UI requirements. The blanket completion claim is too broad. Preserve original receipts for their exact exercised cases.

alternatives: Execute all proposed deletions unchanged: Stop; this removes required loss information, conflates Word review with native persistence, discards type precision and duplicates an existing HTML assertion.
Keep every current abstraction because it has internal consumers: Stop; flat typed persistence and one HTML admission owner can satisfy the jobs with fewer concepts.
Correct the design, preserve earned information and fidelity, and prove exact affected consumers before cuts: Pursue.
Delete all native DOCX state and replace it with a separate JSON artifact: Defer pending explicit disposition of the existing single-file exact-round-trip job; not dead-code cleanup.
proofLimits: Three source/HappyDOM audit probes: 3 pass, 0 fail, 11 assertions, reproducing defective behavior. AI stale acceptance, DOCX cancellation/fitting and detached runtime activation are source findings without fresh browser or native-artifact reproduction. No product change, full suite, bundle, benchmark or upstream research. Proposed persistence flattening is not a compiled replacement. Source reachability is not a bundle measurement or proof of external nonuse.
